messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: HIGH - edge-proxy TLS handshake error rate > 15% in eu-west-1 for the last 3m. Alerting oncall: Jess (oncall). Affected: /generate and /chat routes.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident INC-2026-9876 created and routed to Jess (oncall). Auto-escalation in 5m.

Jess (oncall): acked via PD. Looking into it now. Any recent deploys or cert rotation in eu-west?

Sam: seeing spike in 522/526 from edge -> alb frontends. Cloudwatch: TLS handshake timeout increases, ALB target health shows ~30% unhealthy in tg-prod-eu. Logs show TLS alert: "handshake_failure".

Nikita: interesting — last cert rotate was earlier today for internal session cert, not public cert. Could be SNI mismatch if some proxies still advertising old cert chain.

Luis: FYI I rolled a traffic weight shift at 08:12 UTC: shifted 10% -> eu-west from us-east for perf testing. Could be stressing a subset of targets.

Jess (oncall): ok, priority order: 1) reduce customer impact, 2) identify root cause (cert vs backend), 3) mitigation steps. I'll open a short status note. Sam, can you dump the ALB target details + failing target ids?

Sam: pastebin with target health:
```
TargetGroup: arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:eu-west-1:123456789012:targetgroup/tg-prod-eu/abcd1234
Unhealthy targets: i-0a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b (app-proxy-3), i-0b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c (app-proxy-7)
Health reason: TLS handshake error / connection reset
```

Nikita: curl from inside eu-west edge host to one of the unhealthy targets returns:
```
$ openssl s_client -connect i-0a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b:443 -servername api.prod.redwood
CONNECTED(00000003)
140735...:error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure
```

Luis: not seeing any cert push events in our cert manager logs for those instances. Could be an instance-level nginx change or a kernel-level TLS bug. Any kernel updates?

Jess (oncall): Sam — can you remove the two unhealthy targets from the ALB temporarily to stop the churn, and scale up healthy hosts in eu-west? Do it as a quick mitigation.

Sam: running deregister now: `aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:... --targets Id=i-0a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b Id=i-0b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c`

Sam: deregister completed. Observability shows error rate dropping from 18% -> 7% over next 90s. Latency improving.

Jess (oncall): good. That buys time. Nikita, can you check the nginx/TLS config on app-proxy-3? Look for SNI mismatches or cipher list changes.

Nikita: ssh'd into app-proxy-3 — config shows server_name api.prod.redwood and correct cert path (/etc/letsencrypt/live/api.prod.redwood/fullchain.pem). However cert file mtime is 06:05 UTC, service reload at 06:07. But process TLS library shows OpenSSL 1.1.1k with patched ciphers. No obvious mismatch.

Nikita: doing `openssl x509 -in /etc/letsencrypt/live/api.prod.redwood/fullchain.pem -noout -dates` -> cert valid. Huh.

Luis: checking kernel dmesg — I see repeated 'TLS: decryption failed' entries on app-proxy-7 around 08:11 UTC. Could be a library regression from a rolling update earlier this week.

Jess (oncall): Arjun (Infra Lead) — looping you in. Do we have any pending package updates that could affect TLS stacks?

Infra Lead (Arjun): noted. We did a minor OpenSSL backport to a subset of hosts last week, but it was intentionally staged. Will check canary results. If it's the backport, we should revert on the affected hosts.

Sam: to confirm, the unhealthy hosts are only the ones that received the backport? Checking tags... yes: app-proxy-3 and app-proxy-7 have `tls-backport=v2`. Other hosts show `tls-backport=v1` and are healthy.

Nikita: that matches. Hypothesis: backport v2 changes default cipher ordering causing handshake failures with some client ALB frontends.

Jess (oncall): action plan: 1) keep deregistered hosts out of rotation, 2) rollback tls-backport on affected hosts, 3) scale up replacement hosts without v2, 4) monitor for errors and re-register when healthy.

Arjun: I'll authorize rollback. Sam/Nikita — can you capture a copy of the package list and exact OpenSSL version on the failing hosts before rollback (for postmortem)?

Sam: copied: `openssl version -a` -> OpenSSL 1.1.1k-backportv2  11 Jan 2026. Tarball saved to /var/tmp/tls-backport-v2-manifest.txt

Nikita: rolling back now on app-proxy-3 and -7 (systemd stop nginx; yum downgrade openssl libs -> restart).

Nikita: rollback done; TLS library now shows back to 1.1.1k-backportv1. Performing health check...

Sam: re-registering targets after health checks pass (10s grace): `aws elbv2 register-targets --target-group-arn arn:... --targets Id=i-0a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b Id=i-0b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c`

Sam: re-register done. ALB target health -> healthy within 40s. Error rate back to baseline (~1-2%).

Jess (oncall): nice work team. Temporarily rolling back the backport fixed it. Arjun — can we halt further backport rollout until we have a reproducible test?

Arjun: yes, halting rollout. I'll convene a postmortem and a regression test for TLS handshakes with our ALB frontends.

Luis: quick note for status page: impact window 08:10-08:22 UTC, 15-20% of traffic in eu-west degraded. No customer data exposure. Routing mitigation applied.

Jess (oncall): updating incident record and status page now. pd: resolving alert as mitigated; we'll keep monitoring for 30m.

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-2026-9876 status changed to: Mitigated by Jess (oncall).

Sam: leaving monitoring runbook checks in place. I'll follow up with exact host list and package diffs for the postmortem.

Nikita: will write up repro steps. We should add an automated handshake test in our CI that runs openssl s_client against a staging ALB with both cipher orderings.

Jess (oncall): agreed. Thanks everyone. Stand down unless PD re-escalates. :thumbsup:
